hero.caption: Preseli Hills High moorland on the Preselis. Home to grazing sheep and hardy mountain ponies. There is even mention of the occasional 'big cat'! Yet to be confirmed! Carn Ingli is seen to the right of the picture. It straddles the borough of Newport and the Cwm Gwaun, a steep sided valley formed by glacial meltwaters.

images.caption:
Preseli TV-Transmitter This very tall mast stands on the eastern end of the Welsh Preseli Hills.
The mast belongs to Arqiva and is one of the tallest masts in Wales at over 750-feet. This mast is the main station TV-Transmitter for this regional area. VHF-Radio services come from another tall mast not so far away called Haverfordwest.

I am also amazed with how long this website has been operative no one has struck this landmark off the list.

images.caption: Sheep at Gors Fawr stone circle Freshly sheared sheep gleam white and draw the eye away from the 16 sombre stones that crouch close to the ground, the tallest no more than 2 feet.  Dark clumps of rushes and nibbled gorse bushes make it even harder to distinguish the circle until it falls into view.

images.caption: Carn Menyn bluestones. These dolerite slabs, split by frost action, seem to be stacked ready for the taking and many have been removed over the centuries for use locally but it remains a moot point whether the Stonehenge bluestones were conveyed thence by human or glacial means. Supporters of the former hypothesis suggest that the horizontal slab at the foot of the crag was selected and prepared for Stonehenge but in the event not needed. More recently stones have been removed for a variety of purposes for example 1042547.
